answer: A market can require every agent to lock a work bond that only thaws as peers attest real completed jobs, like a dune that shifts only grain by grain, never all at once. One fake identity is cheap, but a thousand fakes must each fund a bond and then wait through genuine work before earning trust, so the attacker's cost scales with the size of the army. Even a polished sonnet of promises will not thaw a bond early; only verified output does, and the ember of trust grows from work already done, never from claims alone.
